Entries.Text: Find the header, dummies, materials, bones and meshes of the loaded model by their names, fields and values. Fill in any of the inputs: empty ones are ignored, and the rest must all match. Click a result to select it.

Find models, and the dummies, materials, bones and meshes within them, across every model of the project. Fill in any of the inputs: empty ones are ignored, and the rest must all match. Models with unsaved edits are searched as they are in the editor. Click a result to load its model and select it.
Load a model to search it.
Search the loaded model only, or every model of its file (a part or map binder can hold several).
Search every model of the project, or only one list of the Source List. A search of every model reads each file, so it can take a while; narrowing it here, or giving a model name, makes it quicker.
Matches the model name, the name of the file holding it, or its alias. Given on its own, the models themselves are listed.
Matches the kind of object (Header, Dummy, Material, Node or Bone, Mesh) or its name: a bone or material by name, a dummy by reference ID, a mesh by position.

Matches the name of a field, as the Properties view shows it. Nested fields are named by their path, such as Textures[0].Path or BoundingBox.Min; the last part alone matches too. Meshes also have VertexCount.
Matches the value of any field, or the name of an enum value. When a field is also given, the value must be in that field. Vectors are written x, y, z and lists of indices as 1, 2, 3.
The ends of the range. Either can be left empty.
The value contains the text, or the name of its enum entry does.
The value is the same. Numbers are compared as numbers, so 1 matches 1.0 but not 10.
The value is not the same. Numbers are compared as numbers.
The value is a number within the range, including both ends. Either end can be left empty.
The value is a number, compared with the one given. True and false count as 1 and 0.
Inputs must equal the text rather than be contained in it. Numbers are compared as numbers, so 1 finds 1.0.
Run the search, or start over.
Runs the search. Leaving an input after changing it, or pressing Enter in it, does the same.
Empties the inputs and the results.
The search runs in the background. Results are listed as they are found.
Stops the search. The results found so far are kept.
Click a result to jump to it. The filter narrows the list down without searching again.
Over {0} results; only the first {0} are shown. Narrow the search to see the rest.
The search result no longer exists. Search again.
